rules.rule:
Each instruction must examine each account before it reads or writes that account. It must examine:
- the owner
- the signer flag
- the writable flag
- the PDA address, derived again with create_program_address and the bump
- the discriminator, before a typed load
Report a new or changed handler that does not do all of these checks. Also report a new account in a handler that does not get all of these checks.
Source: SDLC 3.4.1 and the PR template checklist.

Program code must not panic. Outside #[cfg(test)] code, report:
- unwrap, expect, panic!, unreachable! and todo!
- a slice or array index that can go out of bounds
- integer + - * / without a check, when a value comes from input or account data
- an `as` cast that can truncate a value
Use checked arithmetic, get() and try_from. Return an error.
Source: SDLC 3.2.8 and SCC-SEC-008.

Parsers for reports, CBOR, COSE, DER and JWT must:
- examine the length before each slice
- have a limit on recursion and on each loop
- return Result
Report a change that increases or removes MAX_CBOR_SKIP_DEPTH, MAX_NITRO_DOCUMENT_LEN or MAX_CERT_DER_LEN. Report a read from an SNP report that is shorter than 1,184 bytes (SnpReportView).
Source: SCC-SEC-008.

Read these values only from the signed report or document bytes:
- measurement
- REPORT_DATA
- chip_id
- TCB version
- enclave public keys
Do not read them from instruction data. Do not read them from a struct that the caller supplies. Report a change that reads one of these values from an unsigned source.
Source: high-level design, section 4.5.

Verification must fail closed. Report a path that returns success in one of these conditions:
- The program did not verify a signature.
- The expected precompile instruction (EXPECTED_SIGVERIFY_PROGRAM_ID or the native secp256r1 program) is missing.
- The precompile instruction verifies a different message.
- The backend source or the report version is unknown.
- A Mode B call has no nonce.
Also report unwrap_or_default or a fallback value on Clock or on a different sysvar.
Source: SCC-SEC-003 and SCC-SEC-004.

Report a change that makes one of these checks less strict:
- SNP policy bit 19 (DEBUG) is 0.
- SNP policy bit 18 (MIGRATE_MA) is 0.
- SNP policy bit 17 is 1.
- VMPL is 0.
- The report version is in 1..=5.
- signature_algo is 1.
- The program rejects an all-zero measurement.
- The signed measurement is on the BackendPolicy allowlist for its source.
- The TCB floor applies.
- TDX rejects a debug QE (ATTRIBUTES.FLAGS bit 1).
- TDX rejects a debug TD (TD_ATTRIBUTES bit 0).
Source: SCC-SEC-001 and SCC-SEC-002.

Report a change to one of these rules:
- An attestation is not older than 150 slots.
- Slot hashes come only from the real SlotHashes sysvar address.
- The UsedNonceAccount PDA seeds stay the same.
- Each path that uses a nonce rejects the legacy 17-byte record and the 49-byte record with NonceAlreadyUsed.
- close_stale_nonce closes a record only after 150 slots.
- close_stale_nonce sends the lamports only to the recorded refund_pubkey.
- The TDX challenge tombstone (expires_slot = 0) is permanent.
- Mode B introspection accepts only a top-level call frame (InvalidConsumerStackHeight).
Source: SCC-SEC-004 and SCC-SEC-005.

These five parts must use the same V3 action_hash encoding:
- the verifier
- the CPI helpers
- the Rust SDK
- the TypeScript SDK
- the sidecar function screen_transaction
The contract is in section 4 of crates/solana-confidential-compute-cpi/README.md. Report a pull request that does one of these things:
- It changes the encoding in some of the five parts, but not in all of them.
- It adds a fallback to V1 or V2 digests.
- It removes duplicate accounts from the hash.
- It removes the effective signer and writable flags from the hash.
- It calculates the hash before the final message has its payer and accounts.
Source: SCC-SEC-006.

Always report a change to MILAN_ARK_MODULUS, AWS_NITRO_ROOT_CA_PUBKEY_XY, EXPECTED_SIGVERIFY_PROGRAM_ID or a declare_id! program ID. Ask for the source of the new value.
Also report a change that does one of these things:
- It makes the PolicyRegistry.authority signer check less strict.
- It lets rotate_root_cert do more than refuse the request.
- It lets init_policy_registry run without the loader-owned ProgramData account.
- It lets init_policy_registry run without the current upgrade authority as signer.
- It lets rotate_authority run without signatures from both authorities.
- It lets a policy update decrease a TCB component.
- It allows more than eight legacy measurements.
Source: SECURITY.md, section "Administrative authorities and trust roots".

Deployed accounts keep their old layout. Report a change to one of these items:
- an account size
- a field offset
- a discriminator
- a report byte offset
Report the change only if the pull request does not tell how existing accounts and clients migrate.

Mocks must not get into a real deployment. Report a change that does one of these things:
- It lets the mock-crypto feature build for Solana SBF.
- It makes `just sbf-mock-guard` less strict, or removes it.
- It makes test-utils or test-bpf a default feature.
- It lets the sidecar use the mock provider or synthetic evidence when dry_run is false (fail_closed_live_mock).

Signing key material must derive Zeroize and ZeroizeOnDrop. The sidecar must drop the old key when it rotates the key.
Report code that does one of these things with key material:
- It writes the key to a log.
- It formats the key with Debug or Display.
- It serializes the key.
- It returns the key over HTTP.
- It writes the key to disk.
The API must stay on loopback. Report a change to the 127.0.0.1:8080 default or to validate_loopback_addr.
Before the sidecar releases a signature, it must run screen_transaction in server.rs (SCC-SIDECAR-001) on the complete transaction. Report a path that does not do this. Also report a change that makes screen_transaction or validate_compute_budget in signing_policy.rs less strict.
Source: SCC-SEC-007.

Pin each third-party action to a full commit SHA, with a version comment. Give each workflow a permissions block with the minimum permissions.
Report:
- pull_request_target together with a checkout of the pull request head
- secrets that go to untrusted code
- secrets that go into logs
- a publish step that uses a long-lived token and not OIDC trusted publishing
Source: SDLC 3.4.5 and 6.3.

Report one of these items if the pull request description does not give a reason for it under "New dependencies":
- a new dependency
- a git source or a path source
- a registry that is not crates.io or npm
A new dependency of the verifier program, core, crypto, cpi or the sidecar needs an acknowledgment from the security team (PR template).

Some changes alter behavior that a document describes. Examples are an error code, a PDA seed, an account layout, a limit or a @spec clause. These documents describe behavior:
- SECURITY.md
- docs/intent/confidential-compute-verifier-specs.md
- docs/high-level-design.md
- the crate README files
The same pull request must update the document. Report the passage that is not correct.
Source: SDLC 3.4.1.

Tell the author when a change can increase compute units on a hot path. assert_attestation_atomic must use 2,500 CU or less (SCC-CONSUMER-002). The measured Mode A consumer check uses 355 CU. When a verification path changes, ask for the output of `just compute-regression`.
